subject: Privacy onboarding checklist and audit scope for Medipartner
messages:
From: Lena Koval <lena.koval@medipartner.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@medipartner.com>, Medipartner Legal <legal@medipartner.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Privacy onboarding: DPIA, Art.28/30 docs, and audit rights

Hi Alex / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — Medipartner is moving quick and I started the internal privacy checklist. Our legal/privacy team has a few items we need to tick off before production access:

- A short DPIA summary for how Redwood will process patient-identifiable metadata (we'll need enough detail to include in our internal DPIA).
- Art. 28 & 30 artifacts: processing activities register excerpt, the Data Processing Addendum, and any Art. 28 annex/processor controls.
- Full list of current subprocessors and the typical method for notifying customers of new subprocessors.
- Data transfer mechanisms (SCCs / EU adequacy / other safeguards).
- Scope and process for customer audit rights — remote evidence vs on-site; what evidence Redwood will provide and typical timelines.

I've attached our vendor questionnaire (vendor_questionnaire_medipartner.pdf) with a few scored items. Can you confirm what you can provide directly vs what will need an NDA/SOW? Also, can we schedule a 30-min call Thursday to review?

Appreciate it — aim to finalize the package next week.

Best,
Lena
Privacy Lead, Medipartner Health

Attachment: vendor_questionnaire_medipartner.pdf (pdf)
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Koval <lena.koval@medipartner.com>, Oliver Smith <oliver.smith@medipartner.com>, Medipartner Legal <legal@medipartner.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Privacy onboarding: DPIA, Art.28/30 docs, and audit rights

Marissa / Karthik — looping you in to confirm our standard artifacts and any deviations for a healthcare customer storing metadata. Summary of ask from Medipartner (see Lena's note below): DPIA summary, Art.28/30 artifacts, subprocessor roster, transfer safeguards, and audit scope.

Rough proposal from our side:
- Provide a concise DPIA summary (1-2 pages) that outlines processing purposes, categories of personal data, lawful basis, data flows, retention, and key mitigations (pseudonymization, access controls, logging). We should flag any areas where customer-specific config affects scope.
- Share DPA (redacted) + Art.28 Annex (we maintain a standard annex describing controls). I can attach the current annex draft (Art28_Annex_v3.docx) — will need legal sign-off for any changes.
- Subprocessor roster: provide current list and our notification cadence (30 days notice for new subprocessors; immediate listing in portal). We must confirm whether Medipartner requires explicit opt-in for new subprocessors or mere notice.
- Transfers: we use SCCs for transfers from EU to US in standard customer deployments; we can provide a copy of the executed SCCs and mapping of where data is stored/processed.
- Audit rights: our standard is to provide evidence via a secure evidence portal (logs, policy artifacts, SOC2 excerpts) and to support one remote/virtual audit per 12 months. On-site audits are allowed in high-assurance contracts but require scheduling, scope docs, and a 60-day lead time and usually an NDA/scope SOW. We should confirm Medipartner's expectations on on-site.

Karthik — can you prepare SOC2 excerpt (redacted) and an operations summary (retention, access logs, KMS usage) that we can share? Marissa — please review the annex and proposed audit language; we should avoid committing to unconstrained on-site access.

I'll draft a customer-facing reply with attachments and propose a Thursday 30-min slot with you both on the call.

Thanks,
Alex
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

(Attachment stubs to prepare: redwood_art28_annex_v3.docx, soc2_excerpts_redacted.pdf)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Koval <lena.koval@medipartner.com>, Medipartner Legal <legal@medipartner.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Privacy onboarding: DPIA, Art.28/30 docs, and audit rights

Alex / Karthik — thanks for the summary. A few edits and clarifications from Legal & Privacy:

- DPIA: We'll produce a 2-page DPIA summary tailored to Medipartner's described processing. It will include a high-level data flow diagram (figure), retained as an annex in the packet. For a full joint DPIA we typically offer a paid workshop (SOW).
- Art.28 Annex: I attached Art28_Annex_v3.docx (minor edits). This annex includes our technical/organizational measures, subprocessors, and standard audit language. Please don't share any unredacted internal runbooks.
- Subprocessors: Our current roster includes cloud infra provider, observability provider, and a managed database host — we'll provide names and subprocessor contacts. Notification policy is 30 days. If they require opt-in rather than notice, we need to escalate commercially.
- Transfers: SCCs by default; for highly regulated customers we have a contractual Addendum that references additional safeguards (encryption at rest, contractual commitments around access controls).
- Audit rights: Legal-approved language below (suggested to customer):

  "Customer may request evidence of Redwood's compliance with the Processor obligations (including redacted SOC2 report excerpts, control policies, and sample logs). Remote evidence will be provided within fifteen (15) business days of a documented request. On-site audits require a formal request, execution of an NDA, and a negotiated SOW covering scope/resourcing; Redwood will not accept unlimited operational access and reserves the right to redact third-party confidential information."

Karthik — please add the SOC2 excerpt and a short ops note on log retention/availability. Once we have those I can sign off and Alex can respond to Medipartner with the packet and a proposed call time.

-Marissa
Head of Privacy & Legal, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Art28_Annex_v3.docx (docx)

Hi Lena / Oliver — thanks for the checklist and apologies for the back-and-forth. Please find what we can provide immediately:

Attachments we can share now (stubs attached to this email):
- redwood_dpia_summary_medipartner.pdf (2 pages) — DPIA summary tailored to your described use case.
- redwood_art28_annex_v3.docx — Art.28 annex and technical controls summary.
- soc2_excerpts_redacted.pdf — redacted SOC2 Type II excerpts covering security and logging.
- subprocessor_roster_202705.pdf — current list and contact points.

What we propose for audit/evidence:
- Primary route: secure evidence portal (link provided upon NDA execution) where we deliver redacted SOC2 excerpts, control descriptions, sample logs (timeboxed), and retention artefacts within 15 business days of request.
- On-site: possible but requires NDA + SOW; 60 days' notice recommended. We prefer remote or virtual audits for evidence collection.

Next steps:
1) Marissa & Karthik will host a 30-minute call with your privacy/legal team to walk through the packet and confirm any gaps (proposed slots: Thursday 10:00-10:30 PT or Friday 14:00-14:30 PT).
2) If you need an execution copy of the DPA / SCCs we can circulate for signature; please indicate whether you require any contract-level changes.

If you want the packet in a shared Drive now, tell me and I'll send a secure link.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
